_about: Entries whose identifier was built, trained or tuned on (part of) this benchmark's files — their score is partly accuracy on their own test or training data. Keys are entry-name prefixes; counts are of this benchmark's 637 files, by git blob id. A value is either a text (the whole benchmark is that entry's home turf) or {"why", "cases_tag" or "cases"}: only those cases are; the overall leaderboard then counts the entry, held out, on the other cases.
Pygments: its test suite lexes every one of these files and compares the tokens with a stored golden output (tests/examplefiles/*/*.output): the lexers were written and fixed against them, and the file names match its lexers' patterns. Whether `analyse_text` (the content guesser) was tuned on them is not known — the tests do not check guessing

Chroma.why: 5 of the files are inputs of Chroma's lexer tests (lexers/testdata/*.actual, checked at a6d00fe); many of its lexers are ports of Pygments'

Synid.why: its classifier is Hyperpolyglot's, trained on a 2023 copy of Linguist's samples: 15 of the files are byte-identical to one (tag `seen-in-training`)

Hyperpolyglot.why: classifier trained on a 2023 copy of Linguist's samples: 15 of the files (tag `seen-in-training`)

GitHub Linguist.why: classifier trained on its own samples: 15 of the files are byte-identical to a sample (tag `linguist-sample`; all in Hyperpolyglot's 2023 copy, so in every Linguist release run here)

go-enry.why: generated from Linguist releases that have the same 15 samples (tag `linguist-sample`)
